title: First-touch priming lab notes — warmup & rollout heuristics
content:
Purpose:
This is a ’notes-to-self’ lab doc for first-touch priming (aka warmup) experiments on tenant cohorts. Goal: reduce cold tail latency and KV-cache churn during small initial traffic ramps without adding undue cost or overfitting to synthetic traffic.

Background/context:
- Problem: new tenant or model-flip requests hit empty caches and long setup paths (model load, kernel selection, initial kv-cache filling) -> 95th/99th latency spikes for first ~N requests.
- Tradeoffs: aggressive warmup reduces tail but increases tokens/cost and noise for metrics. Want a cheap, measurable primer that is safe to run from client side or via staged server-side priming.

Running assumptions / constraints:
- Target environments: hosted API (default), Dedicated pools (reserve warmup slot), Private (customer opt-in).
- We only control priming for traffic we route; can't run heavy priming for unknown external clients.
- Instrumentation available: per-request trace id, token_cost estimate, model_variant tag, kv-cache-hit boolean, warmup_flag header, and per-tenant quotas.

Definitions (for this doc):
- first-touch window: first 5m after tenant first successful request or model flip event.
- primer request: synthetic or real request that includes warmup_flag header; expected lightweight prompt (~10–40 tokens) targeting common prefixes.
- effective warmup budget: token cap per tenant for priming (recommended default = 5k tokens).

Prototype recipes (quick wins):
1) Client-initiated mini-prime (opt-in SDK):
   - SDK exposes `client.prime()` which sends 3 short prompts spaced at 10s, 30s, 120s after first call.
   - Prompts are templated: "short assistant init — 1 sentence" (10–20 tokens).
   - Grant: charge to startup-credit bucket (avoid immediate billing shock).
   - Telemetry: attach primer:true, measure kv_cache_hit after each.
   - Rollback: if token_cost > threshold or error_rate spike, disable SDK priming for that region.

2) Server-side quiet priming (controlled route):
   - On detection of tenant-first-touch, schedule 1 background primer request on warm path to the same model variant.
   - Background run should be low-priority (nice) with 30s jitter; do not block user request.
   - Limit: 1 background prime per 2m, total tokens <= effective warmup budget.

3) Shadow mirroring for warmup tuning:
   - Mirror small fraction (0.5–1%) of live requests to a priming runner in a queueless path to observe cold behavior without impacting production latency.
   - Use mirrored responses to compute kv-cache-fill curve.

Priming heuristics and thresholds (tune these):
- If kv_cache_hit rate < 20% for first N requests, run accelerated primer (3 quick primes).
- Stop priming when observed 3 consecutive kv_cache_hit==true or when token budget exhausted.
- Cost cap: default 5k tokens per tenant per 24h for priming; experiments can raise to 10k short term.
- Latency safety: if background priming inflates 95th latency on that pool by >10% from baseline, pause priming and alert.

Telemetry targets (what to measure):
- per-tenant: first-touch start time, primer_token_spend, kv_cache_hit timeline, p50/p95/p99 before vs after primer.
- per-model-variant: average primer effectiveness (reduction in cold p95), primer success rate (no error).
- per-region: primer-induced queueing or CPU/GPU load anomalies.

Experiment matrix ideas:
- Variable: number of primer calls (1, 3, 5), spacing (10s/30s/120s), prompt size (10/30/60 tokens), synthetic vs replayed user prompt.
- Success metric: drop in p95 for first-touch window by >=30% without >5% token-spend increase overall.
- Safety checks: no increase in model-error rate or hallucination frequency for real user traffic.

Safety & Rollback playbook notes:
- Soft-stop: disable priming for affected pool/region automatically if p95 increases > 10% OR error rate increases > 0.5%.
- Fast-rollback: set traffic pin back to previous model variant if anomalies persist >15m.
- Alerting: create dedicated channel #priming-watch with runbook snippets and links to dashboard panel.

Engineering checklist (manual run):
- [ ] Create test tenant with known small traffic generator.
- [ ] Set warmup budget to 10k for this tenant.
- [ ] Enable debug traces and primer:true tag.
- [ ] Run 3 client-side primers, record kv_cache hits and latency curves.
- [ ] Turn on 0.5% shadow mirror for live production and compare.
- [ ] Validate cost impact (<1% token increase overall for pool).

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is the best automated signal for "tenant ready" beyond kv_cache_hit? (consider embedding similarity to common prompts)
- How to handle multi-variant splits where priming one variant will not help another? Option: replicate primer to all active variants in small doses.
- UX: Should SDK expose opt-out by default and ask product teams to opt-in? Likely yes for privacy-conscious customers.

Notes-to-self:
- Try small pilot with Diego's demo tenant next week (JIRA-ENG-1428).
- Hook a lightweight Grafana panel: primer_token_spend / kv_cache_hit over time.
- Consider adding warmup_flag to logs to simplify queries (searchable).

References:
- linked artifacts above (PR 891, JIRA-ENG-1428, page:Priming-playbook).

Random brain dump (for future iterations):
- Could we use a short re-ranking pass as primer (cheap) that warms the attention kernels without generating readable output? Would reduce user-visible cost.
- Maybe a two-tier primer: very cheap kernel-touch followed by 1 small generation if kernel-touch shows successful load.

End of note.
